It stays in the HiBMS FOV until 4/5 of the way through the burn when the HiBMS stops recording data for about 5 seconds. The HiBMS did not record data when the flame extinguished. It was a long burn, with the extinction diameter estimated from the droplet history extrapolated until visible flame extinction using the measured burning rate constant for a short time right before recording stopped.

documents.title: FLEX-154 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-154 Heptane O2 18.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. Almost no residual motion after deployment and ignition. This is a relatively large droplet that stayed in the HiBMS FOV for the entire (short) burn and the entire recording time of the HiBMS IPSU. The droplet radiatively extinguishes after a short burn with no flame oscillations. There is significant post visible flame extinction vaporoization and large vapor cloud formed late in the recording time. The post visible flame extinction behavior is indicative of cool flame burning and extinction.

documents.title: FLEX-155 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-155 Heptane O2 18.0% pressure 102.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet had almost no residual motion after deployment and ignition and stayed in the HiBMS FOV for the entire time images were recorded. The flame had a very short burn time, likely with radiative extinction. There was a high vaporization rate after visible flame extinction, and an eventual plateau late in the HiBMS IPSU recording time coincident with a large vapor cloud. The post visible flame extinction behavior is indicative of cool flame burning and extinction.

documents.title: FLEX-157 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-157 Heptane O2 18.0% pressure 102.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. This is a very small droplet that has a high NW drift velocity in HiBMS FOV. The droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV about 1/3rd of the way through the test. The droplet moves past the NW igniter before the igniter begins to withdraw. The color camera IPSU-4 failed to record any frames after deployment. There is no extinction diameter reported because the droplet is within the HiBMS FOV for such a short fraction of the entire test.

documents.title: FLEX-158 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-158 Methanol O2 18.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. This relatively large droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition and stays in the FOV of all the cameras. The flame oscillates for a few cycles (increasing in magnitude with time) until radiative extinction. The flame is difficult to see with the LLUV because of both the dim flame and the contamination on the LLUV viewing window.

documents.title: FLEX-159 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-159 Methanol O2 18.0% pressure 102.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition and remains near the center of the FOV for the entire test. The flame oscillates for several cycles before radiatively extinguishing. The LLUV flame diameter data has a lot of noise owing to the very dim flames combined with the contamination on the CIR LLUV viewing window.

documents.title: FLEX-160 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-160 Methanol O2 16.0% pressure 102.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.19/0.59/0.25 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet stays with the FOV of all the cameras for the entire burn. The flame diffusively extinguishes. The LLUV images are dim, but the flame size data seems reasonable, but it is a bit noisy. documents.title: FLEX-161 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-161 Methanol O2 16.0% pressure 102.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.16/0.59/0.25 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition and stays within the FOV of all cameras for the entire burn. A long burn to diffusive extinction. The LLUV images are dim and there is a lot of noise in the LLUV flame size data owing to both the dimness of the flame and the contamination of the CIR LLUV viewing window.

documents.title: FLEX-162 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-162 Methanol O2 15.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.54/0.32 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition and remains within the FOV of all the cameras for the duration of the test. The flame oscillates for several seconds with increasing magnitude before radiatively extinguishing. The LLUV images are dim and the LLUV flame data has a lot of noise because of the dimness of the flame and the contamination on the CIR LLUV viewing window.

documents.title: FLEX-163 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-163 Methanol O2 15.0% pressure 102.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.54/0.32 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. documents.title: FLEX-164 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-164 Methanol O2 15.0% pressure 102.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.54/0.32 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The flame oscillates several cycles with nearly constant amplitude before radiatively extinguishing. The LLUV images are dim and the LLUV flame data is noisy as a result of the flame dimness and the contamination of the CIR LLUV viewing window.

documents.title: FLEX-165 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-165 Methanol O2 15.0% pressure 102.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.54/0.32 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition, leaving the droplet shortly after visible flame extinction and then back into the FOV well after extinction near the end of recording. This is a very dim flame with the LLUV data having a lot of noise because of the dimness and the contamination on the CIR LLUV viewing window.

documents.title: FLEX-166 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-166 Heptane O2 18.0% pressure 102.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.670.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. documents.title: FLEX-167 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-167 Methanol O2 14.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.50/0.36 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. documents.text: FLEX-168 Methanol O2 14.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.136/0.50/0.363 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. documents.text: FLEX-169 Methanol O2 21.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.64/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The extinction droplet diameter is the droplet diameter at disruption and not the true extinction droplet diameter.

documents.title: FLEX-170 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-170 Methanol O2 21.0% pressure 102.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.64/0.16 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition. The droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV 3/4ths of the way through the burn and then back into the FOV just after visible flame extinction. The extinction droplet diameter is the droplet diameter when the droplet fully re-appears in the FOV and should be nearly identical to the droplet diameter when the visible flame extinguishes.

The visible flame extinction was followed by rapid vaporization, then plateau when the droplet became quite small. There was a visible vapor cloud formation late in the recording history. The post visible flame extinction behavior is consistent with cool flame burning and extinction.

documents.text: FLEX-223 Methanol O2 12.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.12/0.88 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet deployed and ignited with almost no residual motion. The droplet drifted a little S and then E in the HiBMS FOV, but remained in the FOV of the HiBMS, LLUV and color cameras for the entire recording time.

documents.title: FLEX-224 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-224 Methanol O2 12.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.12/0.88 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts N after deployment and ignition and out of the HiBMS FOV about 3/4ths of the way through the burn. The flame grows, then shrinks in response to the shrinking droplet. The flame is very dim and difficult to see in the LLUV. This is likely diffusive extinction. The extinction droplet diameter results from extrapolating the droplet history to the time the flame extinguishes using the measured burning rate constant while the droplet is within the FOV.

documents.title: FLEX-225 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-225 Methanol O2 12.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.12/0.88 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment/ignition, then starts to drift slowly E, but then chnages direction and quickly drifts W in HiBMS FOV. The droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV about 3/4ths of the way through the burn. The flame is very dim, but does appear to grow, reach a maximum and then decrease in size in response to the shrinking droplet. The extinction droplet diameter is based on extrapolating the droplet history to the time of extinction (as measured by the LLUV) using the burning rate c

documents.title: FLEX-226 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-226 Methanol O2 20.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.20/0.75/0.05 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition, but then starts to drift SE in HiBMS FOV a few seconds after ignition. The droplet drifts out of the HiBMS FOV, but remains in the LLUV and color camera FOVs. The color camera IPSU failed to record any images after deployment. The droplet burns for a relatively long time before a diffusive extinction. The extinction droplet diameter comes from extrapolating the droplet history from the time the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV until extin

documents.title: FLEX-227 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-227 Methanol O2 20.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome unknown Free-floating methanol droplet in a 0.20/0.75.0.05 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The HiBMS IPSU failed to start and thus no droplet data was recorded. The flame was bright and burned for over 5 seconds until a (presumed) diffusive extinction.

documents.title: FLEX-229 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-229 Heptane O2 20.0% pressure 100.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome unknown Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.20/0.75.0.05 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts SE after deployment in the HiBMS FOV, hits the igniter and develops a large drift velocity E. The droplet drifts out of the HiBMS FOV and then the LLUV and color cameras before either extinction or burn-out.

documents.title: FLEX-231 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-231 Methanol O2 19.0% pressure 100.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.19/0.71/0.10 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet has a pronounced drift S in the HiBMS FOV after deployment, strikes the igniter and continues to drift S and out of the HiBMS FOV about 1/3rd of the way through the burn. The droplet burns for a relatively long time to a diffusive extinction. The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment for this test. There is no extinction droplet diameter listed for this test because of the short fraction of the total test the droplet was within the HiBMS FOV.

documents.title: FLEX-232 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-232 Methanol O2 18.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet slowly drifts S after deployment and ignition in the HiBMS FOV, but never leaves the FOV. Diffusive extinction with no disruption.

documents.title: FLEX-233 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-233 Methanol O2 18.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Fiber-supported methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet moves slowly and smoothly W on the fiber in the HiBMS FOV after ignition. The droplet drifts to the edge of the HiBMS FOV, but remains in the FOV. There is some small oscillatory motion on the fiber, but it is a relatively clean burn until diffusive extinction.

documents.title: FLEX-234 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-234 Heptane O2 21.0% pressure 102.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome unknown Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm or nominally air ambient environment. The droplet drifts SE and out of the HiBMS FOV about 1/2 of the way through the burn. The flame begins to oscillate and then drifts S and out of the LLUV FOV before extinction. The Color camera IPSU did not record any images during the burn. It is unclear whether the droplet continued to burn in the LLUV FOV and for how long. The oscillations are significant, but the flame appears to be decreasing in size . From the radiometer, it appears that the droplet burns with a stable flame after th

documents.title: FLEX-235 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-235 Heptane O2 21.0% pressure 102.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome disruption Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm (nominally air) ambient environment. The droplet stays in HiBMS FOV for most of lifetime. The droplet burns to a very small size, with a small disruption coincident with visible flame extinction.

documents.title: FLEX-236 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-236 Heptane O2 21.0% pressure 102.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Fiber-supported heptane droplet burning in a 0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet has oscillations on the fiber throughout the burn, but remains in the HiBMS FOV. Large soot agglomerates interfere with the droplet size measurement for a portion of the burn. The flame radiatively extinguishes after a very long, slow, high amplitude oscillation. This is followed by rapid vaporization with vapor cloud coincident with the plateau. The droplet moves during the vaporization but it doesn't seem to inpact the size measurement significantly. There is a small disruption near the end

documents.title: FLEX-238 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-238 Heptane O2 19.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.19/0.71/0.10 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts N in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition and just out of the FOV before flame extinction/disruption. There may have been a disruption coincident with flame extinction.

documents.title: FLEX-239 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-239 Heptane O2 18.0% pressure 102.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts N after deployment and ignition and out of the HiBMS FOV 1/3rd of the way through the burn. The flame remains in the FOV of both the LLUV and color camera for the duration of the burn. The flame is bright and very luminous from soot oxidation initially, but quickly becomes dimmer blue. The luminosity increases slightly as the flame gets near extinction. Because the droplet is out of the HiBMS FOV for the majority of the test, there is no extinction diameter reported.

documents.title: FLEX-240 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-240 Heptane O2 18.0% pressure 102.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome unknown Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts N after deployment and ignition and out of HiBMS FOV about 1/4th of the way through the burn. The drift velocity is relatively high and the flame is brighter on the leading edge in the direction of the drift. The droplet does stay in the FOV of both the LLUV and Color cameras. There is no extinction diameter for this test because it was in the HiBMS FOV for such a small fraction of the burn. The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment for this test.

documents.title: FLEX-241 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-241 Heptane O2 17.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.17/0.63/0.20 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet has almost no drift after deployment and ignition and stays in the HiBMS, LLUV and color camera FOVs with little motion throughout the IPSU recording time. The flame radiatively extinguishes, there if a brief period after visible flame extinction where the droplet continues to vaporize at a nearly constant rate indicating that there was a cool flame after visible flame extinction. The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.

documents.title: FLEX-242 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-242 Heptane O2 17.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.17/0.63/0.20 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet has almost no drift after deployment and ignition, moving slightly to the SE in the HiBMS FOV but remaining in the FOV of all the cameras for the entire test. The color camera IPSU failed to record any images after deployment. The flame extinguished after approximately 5 sec and that is likely followed by cool flame burning and extinction.

documents.title: FLEX-243 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-243 Heptane O2 17.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome disruption Fiber-supported heptane droplet burning in a 0.17/0.63 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. Neither the HiBMS or color camera IPSUs recorded any images for this test. The droplet burns for a short time to disruption.

documents.title: FLEX-244 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-244 Heptane O2 17.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome burnout Fiber-supported heptane droplet burning in a 0.17/0.63/0.20 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. This is a smaller droplet. After ignition there is a lot of motion on the fiber, not really disruptive burning where the droplet becomes dislodged from the fiber, but the motion clearly influences the burning history. The droplet burned to completion. The color camera did not record to the on-board IPSU for this test.

documents.title: FLEX-245 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-245 Methanol O2 17.0% pressure 100.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome unknown Free-floating methanol droplet in a 0.17/0.63/0.20 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet has a strong N to NE drift after deployment, nearly hitting the ingiter before it withdrew. The droplet has a relatively high drift velocity after ignition and only stays in the HiBMS FOV for a short fraction (1/4th) of the burn. There is no extinction diameter listed because of the short time the droplet is within the FOV. The droplet burns to diffusive extinction.

documents.title: FLEX-246 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-246 Methanol O2 17.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.17/0.63/0.20 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet has almost no drift after deployment and ignition, but then develops a slow drift NE, then E in the color camera FOV shortly into the burn. The droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV near diffusive flame extinction. The extinction droplet diameter comes from extrapolating the droplet history from the time the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV until flame extinction using the measured burning rate constant while the droplet is within the HiBMS FOV. The diameter should be reasonably accurate since the

documents.title: FLEX-247 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-247 Methanol O2 16.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.16/0.59/0.25 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition and remains in the FOV of all the cameras for the entire recording time. It is difficult to say whether this is diffusive or radiative extinction. It is likely near the flammability boundary. The MDCA Color Camera did not record anything beyond droplet deployment on-board for this test.

documents.title: FLEX-248 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-248 Methanol O2 16.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome unknown Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.16/0.59/0.25 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The HiBMS IPSU did not record any images for this test. There was only a very small drift S in color camera FOV, but stays in FOV for entire test (as well as the LLUV FOV). The droplet burned to extinction.

documents.title: FLEX-249 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-249 Heptane O2 16.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.16/0.59/0.25 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. This is a smaller droplet that is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition. It stays in the FOV of all the cameras. The flame surrounding the droplet extinguishes at a very small size, near the limit of what we can reasonably measure. The flame size is nearly constant throughout the burn, decreasing only slightly towards the end of the burn after only slightly increasing in size initially. The flame standoff increases linearly throughout the burn.

documents.title: FLEX-250 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-250 Methanol O2 15.0% pressure 100.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Fiber-supported methanol droplet burning in a 0.15/0.55/0.30 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. There is a small amount of axial motion on the fiber, but it doesn't seem to influence the burning behavior to a large degree. This is a relatively short, transient burn; likely radiative extincion.

documents.title: FLEX-251 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-251 Methanol O2 15.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.15/0.55/0.30 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition. It remains in the FOV for the duration of the burn, leaving shortly after visible flame extinction. This ambient environment is likely near flammability boundary so it is difficult to determine whether it was diffusive or radiative extinction.

documents.title: FLEX-252 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-252 Methanol O2 14.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.51/0.35 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet has a slow SE drift in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition. The droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV well after visible flame extinction, but then drifts back into the HiBMS FOV before the end of the recording period. The droplet burned for a short time before flame extinction.

documents.title: FLEX-253 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-253 Methanol O2 14.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.51/0.35 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition in the HiBMS FOV. It starts to drift S as it burns and leaves the FOV well after visible flame extinction. The droplet burns for only a very short time and the flame is very dim, almost undetectable in both the LLUV and Color Cameras. The droplet is very near or even below the flammability limit.

documents.title: FLEX-254 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-254 Methanol O2 13.0% pressure 101.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.13/0.47/0.40 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet stays in HiBMS FOV for the entire recording period. Very short burn to extinction. This is likely below the flammability limit.

documents.title: FLEX-255 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-255 Heptane O2 24.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient envrionment. The droplet drifts out of HiBMS FOV (but remains in the FOV of the LLUV and Color Camera) close to extinction. There is a small vapor cloud formed at extinction. There is noise in the analysis of the droplet image because of soot particles formed during combustion that interfere with the analysis. It is unclear whether this is radiative or diffusive extinction or if there was a cool flame after visible flame extinction.

documents.title: FLEX-256 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-256 Heptane O2 23.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.23/0.52/0.25 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts E after deployment and ignition in the HiBMS FOV leaving the FOV just prior to extinction or burnout. The droplet burns to a very small size and then appears to disrupt or rapidly change direction after the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV. The extinction droplet diameter comes from extrapolating the droplet history from the time it leaves the FOV until flame extinction using the measured burning rate constant. The small extinction droplet size suggests that the droplet burned almos

documents.title: FLEX-257 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-257 Methanol O2 24.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts SE in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition. It stops briefly at the corner of the FOV and then disappears from the FOV (there one frame, gone the next) at a time coincident with visible flame extinction. The droplet may have moved to just outside the FOV after the flame extinguished. The droplet burned nicely to a diffusive extinction. The extinction droplet diameter is the droplet diameter in the frame just before the droplet disappears.

documents.title: FLEX-258 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-258 Methanol O2 24.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Fiber-supported methanol droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet remains in the HiBMS FOV but there is a lot of motion on the fiber and eventually the droplet disrupts and becomes dislodged from the fiber. There is no extinction droplet diameter reported as a result of the disruption.

documents.title: FLEX-259 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-259 Methanol O2 23.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet in a 0.23/0.52/0.25 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts SE in the HiBMS FOV after ignition and out of FOV right near diffusive extinction. The extinction droplet diameter is extrapolated from the droplet history from the time the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV until visible flame extinction using the burning rate constant from the last part of the burn while the droplet is within the FOV.

documents.title: FLEX-260 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-260 Methanol O2 23.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Fiber-supported methanol droplet burning in a 0.23/0.52/0.25 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet remains in the HiBMS FOV and there is very little motion on the fiber until very close to visible flame extinction when the droplet gets dislodged from the fiber. Because flame extinction occurs when the droplet disrupts off of the fiber, there is not extinction droplet diameter listed.

documents.title: FLEX-261 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-261 Methanol O2 21.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet in a 0.21/0.49/0.30 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts NW in the HiBMS FOV after deployment, hits the igniter and then drifts quickly S after ignition. The droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV shortly after ignition so only a small portion of the droplet burning history is captured. It also leaves the color camera FOV. Because only a short part of the burning history is captured, there is no extinction droplet diameter listed and the burning rate constant is likely inaccurate.

documents.title: FLEX-262 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-262 Methanol O2 21.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet in a 0.21/0.49/0.30 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts SE in the HiBMS FOV after deployment, hits the igniter then begins to drift slowly NW after ignition. The droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV before extinction, but most of the burning history is captured by the HiBMS. The droplet burns for a long time before diffusive extinction. The extinction droplet diameter is extrapolated fom the droplet size history from the time the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV until visible flame extinction using the measured burning rate constant from the time perio

documents.title: FLEX-263 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-263 Methanol O2 21.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Fiber-supported methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.49/0.30 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts slowly E along the fiber in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition. There is a little disruptive motion on the fiber during the burning history. This is a diffusive extinction.

documents.title: FLEX-264 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-264 Heptane O2 21.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet in a 0.21/.0.49/0.30 O2/N2/He, 0.7 atm ambient environment. The droplet stays in HiBMS FOV for the entire test. The flame grows to a maximum size shortly after ignition and then stays at a constant size until flame extinction. It is unclear whether this is diffusive or radiative extinction. There is no evidence of prolonged cool flame burning after visible flame extinction (no rapid vaporization after or vapor cloud formation in the color camera).

documents.title: FLEX-265 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-265 Heptane O2 21.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.21/0.49/0.30 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet stays in the HiBMS FOV (and the FOV of all the cameras) for the entire test. The flame grows, reaches a maximum size and then decreases in size until diffusive extinction at a very small size. Shortly after extinction, the droplet appears to disrupt and disappears from the HiBMS FOV.

documents.title: FLEX-266 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-266 Heptane O2 20.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.20/0.45/0.35 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet stays in HiBMS FOV (and the FOV of all cameras) for the entire test. The flame grows continusously after ignition, radiatively extinguishing after approximately 5 seconds. Ther appears to be no cool flame or only a very brief one (no significant vaporization after extinction and also no vapor cloud formation in the color camera view).

documents.title: FLEX-267 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-267 Heptane O2 20.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.20/0.45/0.35 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet remains in the HiBMS FOV (and the FOV of all the cameras) for the entire test. The flame grows throughout the test and gets dimmer until radiatively extinguishing after approximately 5 seconds. There appears to be no evidence of cool flame formation (no rapid vaporization after visible flame extinction and no vapor cloud formed in the color camera view).

documents.title: FLEX-268 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-268 Methanol O2 20.0% pressure 69.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.20/0.45/0.35 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition, but remains within the FOV for the entire test. A very dim flame barely detectable in the Color Camera. Very long burn resulting in diffusive extinction, although the flame standoff grows throughout the test.

documents.title: FLEX-269 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-269 Methanol O2 20.0% pressure 69.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.20/0.45/0.35 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition, drifts around the HiBMS FOV, but remains in the FOV for the entire burn and well after visible flame extinction.

documents.title: FLEX-270 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-270 Methanol O2 18.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.42/0.40 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition, leaving the FOV when the visible flame extinguishes. This was a large droplet and likely radiative extinction.

documents.title: FLEX-271 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-271 Methanol O2 18.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.42/0.40 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts N in the HiBMS FOV after deployment, then hits the igniter and drifts E and out of the FOV before extinction. The extinction droplet diameter is extrapolated from the droplet history from the point the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV until the time of visible flame extinction using the measured burning rate constant during the later period while the droplet is in the HiBMS FOV.

documents.title: FLEX-272 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-272 Methanol O2 18.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Fiber-supported methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.42/0.40 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. There is almost no axial motion of the droplet relative to the fiber, but the droplet does oscillate radially on the fiber which causes minor disruptions in the flame and creates some scatter in the droplet history.

documents.title: FLEX-273 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-273 Heptane O2 18.0% pressure 69.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.42/0.40 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts NE in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition, but remains in the FOV of all cameras for the entire test. The droplet burns for several seconds, the flame grows, reaches a maximum size and remains nearly constant for the entire test. The luminosity of the flame continuously decreases as the droplet burns. This is likely near the flammability limit. There is no evidence of cool flame formation (no rapid vaporization or vapor cloud formation).

documents.title: FLEX-274 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-274 Heptane O2 18.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.42/0.40 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts NE after deployment and ignition, but remains in HiBMS FOV for duration of the burn and several seconds after flame extinction (long enough to observe the vaporization history). The flame grows slightly reaches a maximum size 1/3rd of the way through the burn and then decreases in size in response to the shrinking droplet. This is likely diffusive extinction, but very close to the flammability limit. There is no evidence of a cool flame (rapid vaporization after visible flame ex

documents.title: FLEX-275 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-275 Heptane O2 17.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.17/0.38/0.45 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts NE in the HiBMS FOV, but stays in the FOV for the entire test. Well after flame extinction, the droplet drifts partially out of the HiBMS FOV and then back in for the remainder of the recording time. The flame grows continuously throughout the test getting dimmer until the flame extinguishes. There is no evidence of a cool flame (continued vaporization or vapor cloud).

documents.title: FLEX-276 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-276 Heptane O2 17.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Fiber-supported heptane droplet burning in a 0.17/0.38/0.45 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet exhibits significant axial and radial oscillations throughout the test. The burning rate and extinction diameter data are strongly influenced by this motion. The residual droplet on the fiber has a large gas bubble that results in the size jump after visible flame extinction.

documents.title: FLEX-277 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-277 Methanol O2 17.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.17/0.38/0.45 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts S in HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition and out of FOV, but well after extinction.

documents.title: FLEX-278 (Methanol)
documents.text: FLEX-278 Methanol O2 17.0% pressure 70.9kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Fiber-supported methanol droplet in a 0.17/0.38/0.45 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet migrates slowly W in the HiBMS FOV after ignition but remains in the FOV the entire test. There is a small spot on fiber burns off early in burn. A short burn to extinction. This is near the LOI in this ambient mixture.

documents.title: FLEX-279 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-279 Heptane O2 21.0% pressure 102.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm (nominally air) ambient environment. The droplet stays in HiBMS FOV (it briefly drifts out well after visible flame extinction) for the entire test. This test likely had a cool flame following visible flame extinction. There was a large vapor cloud formed at the end of the test.

documents.title: FLEX-280 (Heptane)
documents.text: FLEX-280 Heptane O2 21.0% pressure 102.3kPa flow Nonecm/s outcome extinction Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.21/0.15/0.64 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet drifts E in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition and out of the FOV right before diffusive extinction. The extinction droplet diameter comes from extrapolating the droplet history from the time it leaves the FOV until visible flame extinction using the measured burning rate constant from the last part of the burn.

documents.title: Space Experiment Concepts: Cup-Burner Flame Extinguishment
documents.text: Space Fire Suppression Processes & Technology. Space experiment concepts of cup-burner flame extinguishment have been conceived to address to the key issues (i.e., organizing questions) in space fire suppression. Cup-burner flame extinguishment experiment can reveal physical and chemical suppression processes and provide agent effectiveness data useful for technology development of space fire suppression systems in various reduced-gravity platforms.

documents.title: Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus - Flame Extinguishment Experiment
documents.text: Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus Flame Extinguishment Experiment (MDCA-FLEX) will assess the effectiveness of fire suppressants in microgravity and quantify the effect of different possible crew exploration atmospheres on fire suppression. The goal of this research is to provide definition and direction for large scale fire suppression tests and selection of the fire suppressant for next generation crew exploration vehicles.

documents.title: Detailed Results from the Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) March 2009 to December 2011
documents.text: The Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) program is a continuing set of experiments on droplet combustion, performed employing the Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA), inside the chamber of the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), which is located in the Destiny module of the International Space Station (ISS). This report describes the experimental hardware, the diagnostic equipment, the experimental procedures, and the methods of data analysis for FLEX. It also presents the results of the first 284 tests performed. The intent is not to interpret the experimental results but rather to make them available to the entire scientific community for possible future interpretations.

documents.title: Skylab Experiment M-479: Zero Gravity Flammability
documents.text: Flammability under conditions of weightlessness was investigated in Skylab 4. Thirty-seven experiments using six materials were successfully carried out to learn how a flame acts in the absence of convection. Specific objectives were to measure the extent of surface flame propagation and flash-over to adjacent materials, rates of surface and bulk flame propagation, self-extinguishment, and extinguishment by both vacuum and water spray. Data were returned in the form of crew comments on voice tapes and sixteen millimeter motion pictures taken at 24 frames per second. All experiments were performed and all hardware functioned properly, although an operational oversight caused the water in the supply tank to be less than the minimum required pressure. Burning rates were significantly reduced as anticipated from earlier aircraft tests. Some reduction of total burning was also noted. The surface burn was not followed by continued inward burning as typically experienced on Earth although some one-g tests at extremely low pressures have partially reproduced this condition. Ignition and extinguishment also appear to be similar to one-g. A soft blue flame was seen by the crew, but was not detected on the film emulsions used. Smoke patterns were also noted.

documents.title: Skylab Experiment M479 Zero Gravity Flammability
documents.text: Flammability under conditions of weightlessness was investigated in Skylab 4. Thirty-seven tests using six materials were successfully carried out to learn more about how a flame acts in the absence of convection. Specific objectives were to note the extent of surface flame propagation and flash-over to adjacent materials, rates of surface and bulk flame propagation, self-extinguishment, and extinguishment by both vacuum and water spray. All tests were performed and all hardware functioned properly, although an operational oversight caused the water in the supply tank to be less than the minimum required pressure. Burning rates were significantly reduced as anticipated from earlier aircraft tests. Some reduction of total burning was also noted. The surface burn was not followed by continued inward burning as typically experienced on earth although some one-g tests at extremely low pressures have partially reproduced this condition. Ignition and extinguishment also appear to be similar to one-g. Smoke patterns were also noted. This can be of value in studying Brownian movement of solids in gases under conditions of weightlessness.

documents.title: Self Induced Buoyant Blow Off in Upward Flame Spread on Thin Solid Fuels
documents.text: Upward flame spread experiments were conducted on a thin fabric cloth consisting of 75% cotton and 25% fiberglass. The sample is sandwiched symmetrically with stainless steel plates with the exposed width varying between 2 to 8.8 cm from test to test and >1.5m tall. The bottom edge was ignited resulting in a symmetric two sided flame. For the narrower samples (. 5cm), two sided flame growth would proceed until reaching some limiting value (15-30 cm depending on sample width). Fluctuation or instability of the flame base on one side would initially become visible and then the flame base would retreat downstream and cause extinguishment on one side. Detailed examination of the still images shows that the fuel continues to vaporize from the extinguished side due to the thermally thin nature of the fuel. But, due to the remaining inert fiberglass mesh, which acts as a flashback arrestor, the extinguished side was not able to be reignited by the remaining flame. The remaining flame would then shrink in length due to the reduced heat transfer to the solid to a shorter length. The one-sided flame will spread stably with a constant speed and a constant flame length to the end of the sample. A constant length flame implies that the pyrolysis front and the burnt out fronts move at the same speed. For the wider samples (. 7cm), no one-sided extinction is observed. Two-sided flames spread all the way to the top of the sample. For these wider widths, the flames are still growing and have not reached their limiting length if it exists. Care was taken to minimize the amount of non-symmetries in the experimental configuration. Repeated tests show that blow-off can occur on either side of the sample. The flame growth is observed to be very symmetric during the growth phase and grew to significant length (>10cm) before extinction of the flame on one side. Our proposed explanation of this unusual phenomenon (i.e. stronger two ]sided flame cannot exist but weaker one-sided flame can) is as follows: The observed one-sided extinction is a blow- off induced by buoyant entrainment. It is known that the flammable diffusion flame regime is bounded by quenching and blow ]off limits when varying incoming air velocity. The narrowest samples tested (between 2 and 5 cm) begin within the flammable range, but as the flame grows, the buoyancy driven air velocity increases at the neighborhood of the flame base. The initially stable flame crosses the extinguishment boundary resulting in a flame blow-off. When one-side of the flame extinguishes, the remaining side shrinks due to the reduced heat transfer to the solid. This reduces the induced velocity and the flame becomes stable. It is proposed that this may have implications to upward flame growth beyond this experiment.

documents.title: Preliminary Results from the Saffire VI Experiment
documents.text: The preliminary results are presented for one test of the last flight of the Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire VI) which was conducted on an orbiting Cygnus spacecraft. These experiments directly address the risks associated with our understanding of spacecraft fire behavior at practical length scales and geometries. The lack of this experimental data has forced spacecraft designers to base their designs and safety precautions on 1-g understanding of flame spread, flame self-extinguishment, fire detection, and suppression. The Saffire experiment was developed by an international team of investigators with the goal of addressing open issues in spacecraft fire safety. NASA’s Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration Project was designed with the goal of conducting a series of large-scale experiments in spacecraft environments that represent practical spacecraft fires. The final flight examined concurrent spread over large samples (all 41 cm wide) including a thin sheet of flammable fuel (cotton/fiberglass 50 cm long); 2-sided spread over  1 cm thick polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) (18 cm long) ; 1-sided spread over 0.5 cm thick (18 cm long); and Nomex fabric (7 cm long).  This paper focusses on the two-sided PMMA sample. The flame heat release is determined and  is compared to the overall temperature rise in the spacecraft and the change in the concentration of carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide in the spacecraft.

documents.title: Buoyant Effects on the Flammability of Silicone Samples Planned for the Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire)
documents.text: Flammability experiments on silicone samples were conducted in anticipation of the Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire). The sample geometry was chosen to match the NASA 6001 Test 1 specification, namely 5 cm wide by 30 cm tall. Four thicknesses of silicone (0.25, 0.36, 0.61 and 1.00 mm) were examined. Tests included traditional upward buoyant flame spread using Test 1 procedures, downward opposed-flow flame spread, horizontal and angled flame spread, and forced-flow upward and downward flame spread. In addition to these configurations, upward and downward tests were conducted in a chamber with varying oxygen concentrations. In the upward buoyant flame spread tests, the flame generally did not burn the entire sample. As thickness was increased, the flame spread distance decreased before flame extinguishment. For the thickest sample, ignition could not be achieved. In the downward tests, the two thinnest samples permitted the flame to burn the entire sample, but the spread rate was lower compared to the corresponding upward values. The other two thicknesses could not be ignited in the downward configuration. The increased flammability for downward spreading flames relative to upward ones is uncommon. The two thinnest samples also burned completely in the horizontal configuration, as well as at angles up to 75 degrees from the horizontal. Upward tests in air with an added forced flow were more flammable. The upward and downward flammability behavior was compared in atmospheres of varying oxygen concentration to determine a maximum oxygen concentration for each configuration. Complementary analyses using EDS, TGA, and SEM techniques suggest the importance of the silica layer deposited downstream onto the unburned sample surface.

documents.title: Buoyant Effects on the Flammability of Silicone Samples Planned for the Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire)
documents.text:
Flammability experiments on silicone samples were conducted in anticipation of the Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire). The sample geometry was chosen to match the NASA 6001 Test 1 specification, namely 5 cm wide by 30 cm tall. Four thicknesses of silicone (0.25, 0.36, 0.61 and 1.00 mm) were examined. Tests included traditional upward buoyant flame spread using Test 1 procedures, downward opposed flow flame spread, horizontal and angled flame spread, forced flow upward and downward flame spread. In addition to these configurations, upward and downward tests were also conducted in a chamber with varying oxygen concentrations. In the upward buoyant flame spread tests, the flame generally did not burn the entire sample. As thickness was increased, the flame spread distance decreased before flame extinguishment. For the thickest sample, ignition could not be achieved. In the downward tests, the two thinnest samples permitted the flame to burn the entire sample, but the spread rate was lower compared to the corresponding upward values. The other two thicknesses could not be ignited in the downward configuration. The increased flammability for downward spreading flames relative to upward ones is uncommon.
